On Oct. 1, 2026:
Subject: RE: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: Oklahoma County District Attorney Office Concerning OCPD Forensic Analyst Elaine Taylor Crime Lab Records
Lisa Erickson Endres, Assistant District Attorney
Oklahoma County District Attorney's Office
211 N. Robinson Ave., Ste. N700
Oklahoma City, OK 73102

October 2, 2026

Via MuckRock (Request No. 199925) and email to Lisa.Endres@oklahomacounty.org<mailto:Lisa.Endres@oklahomacounty.org>

Re: Open Records Act request submitted December 15, 2025, concerning former OCPD Forensic Analyst Elaine Taylor, and the Office's denial letter dated September 18, 2026

Dear Ms. Endres:
I write in response to your letter of September 18, 2026, denying my December 15, 2025, request under the Oklahoma Open Records Act, 51 O.S. §§ 24A.1 et seq. I ask the Office to withdraw the denial, search for responsive records, and produce them or identify the specific statutory exemption applied to each record withheld.
The Office's own Exhibit ORR 1 shows my request went unanswered for 277 days because it was filed away and never forwarded for processing. The grounds stated in the denial do not support withholding every responsive record without a search.
The 277-Day Delay
A public body "must provide prompt, reasonable access to its records." 51 O.S. § 24A.5(6). Any delay "shall be limited solely to the time required for preparing the requested documents and the avoidance of excessive disruptions of the public body's essential functions." Id.
I submitted the request through MuckRock to OCDA@oklahomacounty.org<mailto:OCDA@oklahomacounty.org> on December 15, 2025. MuckRock sent follow-up requests for a response on my behalf to the same address on December 30, 2025, and on January 14, January 29, February 13, March 2, March 17, April 1, April 16, May 1, May 18, June 2, June 17, July 2, July 17, August 3, August 18, September 2, and September 17, 2026. The Office did not acknowledge the request or any follow-up, ask for clarification, or respond in any form until September 18, 2026, 277 days after submission and one day after the final follow-up.
The Office's own exhibit explains the delay. At 11:34 a.m. on September 17, 2026, Brook Arbeitman forwarded the request to you with the note that it "was filed away and not forwarded at the time." The same email noted that "Jennifer Holtzclaw is involved." (Ex. ORR 1.) The Act opens public records "to any person," 51 O.S. § 24A.5, and conditions access on no showing about who the requester is.
No documents were prepared during those 277 days, and the denial letter claims no disruption of the Office's functions. The Office issued the denial the day after the request was located, on grounds that required no search. Section 24A.5(6) allows delay only to prepare the records or to avoid disrupting the Office's work. Leaving the request in a file served neither purpose.
The Act "fixes a mandatory duty" on public officials to provide prompt, reasonable access. Branstetter v. Fallin, No. CV-2014-2372, Journal Entry of Judgment at 4 (Okla. Cnty. Dist. Ct. May 15, 2018). In Branstetter, the Department of Public Safety produced its first records about 11 months after the request and its first emails about 24 months after, and the Governor's office produced its first records about 17 months after. Id. at 3. Neither request had been formally denied. Id. The court entered declaratory judgment that both officials violated the Act by failing to provide prompt and reasonable access, and held that neither the delays "nor the process which resulted in the delays" was prompt or reasonable. Id. at 4.
The Oklahoma Supreme Court has described the Legislature's "emphatic message to government agencies" that, unless records are specifically excluded, "the public must have prompt and reasonable access to records." Okla. Ass'n of Broadcasters, Inc. v. City of Norman, 2016 OK 119, ¶ 15, 390 P.3d 689. The Office produced nothing for 277 days and then denied the request in full.
The Attorney General has advised that a district attorney "has no authority to withhold public records from inspection and copying" and that prompt, reasonable access "generally may include only the time required to locate and compile such public records." 1999 OK AG 58, ¶ 15(2); see id. ¶ 11.
The Stated Grounds for Denial
Ms. Taylor's employer
The letter states that Ms. Taylor was never an employee of the Office, so the Office holds no personnel records about her. The request did not ask for an Office personnel file. It asked for records "in the possession, custody, or control of the Oklahoma County District Attorney's office concerning Elaine Taylor." It named Brady, Giglio, and impeachment determinations, notifications to prosecutors about her credibility or reliability, and communications with district attorneys, defense counsel, and courts concerning her work.
A record under the Act includes any document "created by, received by, under the authority of, or coming into the custody, control or possession of public officials, public bodies, or their representatives." 51 O.S. § 24A.3(1). Records the Office received from OCPD, and records the Office itself created about Ms. Taylor's work and its own disclosure duties, are records of the Office whoever employed her. The request covers any record showing whether and when the Office received records concerning Ms. Taylor from OCPD, including transmittal letters, cover emails, and receipt logs. If the Office holds no such records, I request that you say so.
Identifiable information and time frame
The letter states that the request lacks identifiable information and a time frame. Since November 1, 2025, before this request was submitted, § 24A.5(7) has defined reasonable specificity as a general time frame, identifiable records, and search terms specific enough to help the public body find them. When a request falls short, the public body "may ask the requestor to clarify the request." 51 O.S. § 24A.5(7). Denial for lack of specificity is permitted only after the public body "has engaged with the requestor to seek the information needed to fulfill the request and to identify the records sought." Id.
The Office did not engage. The request asked the Office to "contact me before denying any portion of the request." The Office denied it without contact.
The request also meets each element. It set its time frame as the whole of Ms. Taylor's OCPD employment, including records created before, during, and after it, and stated that she retired in February 2017. It named specific categories of records. It supplied the search term the Office needs, Ms. Taylor's name, with her title and agency.
The letter states that the Office files criminal cases by defendant name, case number, and police incident number. That explanation covers case files. It does not cover email, correspondence with OCPD, Brady and Giglio determinations, or communications with defense counsel and courts, which the request named and which can be searched by Ms. Taylor's name. Section 24A.5(6) allows procedures that protect the organization of records, and it gives a filing system no power to exempt records from the Act. For case files, the relevant case is State v. Holtzclaw, Oklahoma County No. CF-2014-5869, Court of Criminal Appeals No. F-2016-62.
The letter cites 19 O.S. § 215.22 and states that felony files may be destroyed ten years after the last action. The letter does not state that any responsive record has been destroyed. CF-2014-5869 has had appellate and post-conviction activity since judgment, so no ten-year period has run in that case. Ms. Taylor retired in February 2017, and records about her created since then are less than ten years old under any reading of the schedule. If any responsive record has been destroyed, I ask the Office to identify it, the date of destruction, and the authority relied on.
Availability through the court clerk
The letter suggests that responsive material may be found on OSCN or through the Court Clerk. The 2017 filings concerning Ms. Taylor in F-2016-62 were filed under seal and remain sealed under the Court of Criminal Appeals orders of June 8, 2018, and June 14, 2018. They are not available on OSCN. The Office's email, correspondence, and disclosure records were never filed in any court.
The "original source" exemption
The letter cites "51 O.S. §24A.A" for an exemption covering information available from other law enforcement agencies. The Act contains no section by that number. The closest provision is the second sentence of § 24A.20, which allows a law enforcement agency to "deny access to a copy of such a record in an investigative file if the record or a true and complete copy thereof is available for public inspection and copying at another public body." 51 O.S. § 24A.20. That sentence applies only when the same record is open for public inspection and copying somewhere else. The letter identifies no responsive record that OCPD makes available to the public. The 2017 materials concerning Ms. Taylor remain sealed "unless and until" released by the City of Oklahoma City. Holtzclaw v. State, No. F-2016-62, Order Denying Motion to Unseal Proceedings at 1-2 (Okla. Crim. App. June 14, 2018). If the Office relies on a different provision, I ask it to identify the section by number.
A referral to OCPD also leaves the Office's own records unaddressed. Brady and Giglio determinations made by the Office, its correspondence with OCPD, and its communications with defense counsel and courts originated with the Office.

Section 24A.12
Section 24A.12 provides that the district attorney "may keep its litigation files and investigatory reports confidential." The word "may" makes the provision permissive and discretionary. See Mott v. Carlson, 1990 OK 10, ¶ 6 & n.4, 786 P.2d 1247, 1249 & n.4; Falconhead Prop. Owners Ass'n v. Fredrickson, 2002 OK CIV APP 67, ¶ 5, 50 P.3d 224, 226. Exceptions to disclosure are read narrowly in light of the Act's purpose, which is to "ensure and facilitate the public's right of access to and review of government records." 51 O.S. § 24A.2.
The Attorney General reads § 24A.12 the same way: confidentiality of a district attorney's litigation files "is within the discretion of the office involved." 1999 OK AG 58, ¶ 8.
The Supreme Court construes the Act "to allow access unless an exception clearly applies," and "the burden is on the public agency seeking to deny access to show a record should not be made available." Broadcasters, 2016 OK 119, ¶ 15 (citing Citizens Against Taxpayer Abuse, Inc. v. City of Oklahoma City, 2003 OK 65, ¶ 12, 73 P.3d 871, 875). A district attorney's office was a defendant in Broadcasters, and the Court ordered the requested record produced. Id. ¶¶ 23, 31.
A discretionary exemption requires an actual decision by the public body about the records at issue, and that decision is reviewable for abuse of discretion. Ross v. City of Owasso, 2017 OK CIV APP 4, ¶¶ 10-11, 18, 389 P.3d 396, 399-401. In Ross, the court could not review the city's withholding because the city had never decided whether to release the report, and it remanded for a proper response to the request. Id. ¶ 18.
The letter states that the Office "does not elect to disclose any of its investigative files" and that the requested records, "if received, would be part of the District Attorney's investigative file." The Office has not searched for, identified, or reviewed any responsive record. A blanket election over records the Office has not located is no exercise of discretion over them. I ask for a record-by-record determination.
Placing a record in a file does not make it confidential. "Access to records which, under the Oklahoma Open Records Act, would otherwise be available for public inspection and copying, shall not be denied because a public body or public official is using or has taken possession of such records for investigatory purposes or has placed the records in a litigation or investigation file." 51 O.S. § 24A.20. Records the Office received from other public bodies keep whatever status they had when they arrived.
Section 24A.12 covers "litigation files and investigatory reports." Email about an analyst's reliability, Brady and Giglio determinations that apply to an analyst across many cases, and communications with accrediting bodies or oversight agencies are records of a different kind. If the Office places any of them within the litigation file of a particular case, I ask it to identify the case.
Impeachment information the Office has already disclosed to defense counsel or courts in any case has left the Office's control. The Act contains no provision allowing a public body to release a record to some members of the public and withhold it from others.
Finally, "[a]ny reasonably segregable portion of a record containing exempt material shall be provided after deletion of the exempt portions." 51 O.S. § 24A.5(3). The request asked the Office to redact rather than withhold whole documents. The denial withheld everything.
Priority Categories and Search Terms
To speed the search, I identify the following categories for first production. This identification does not narrow or waive the remainder of the December 15, 2025, request.
1. Brady, Giglio, or impeachment determinations, disclosure lists, notices, or memoranda concerning Elaine Taylor, January 1, 2014, to the present.
2. Email and correspondence between the Office and OCPD, including the OCPD Crime Laboratory and the Municipal Counselor's Office, concerning Ms. Taylor's work, testimony, quality reviews, discipline, suspension, or retirement, January 1, 2016, to the present.
3. Communications from the Office to defense counsel or to any court disclosing impeachment information about Ms. Taylor, in any case, January 1, 2014, to the present.
4. Records in the Office's file for State v. Holtzclaw, CF-2014-5869, received from OCPD at any time concerning any review of Ms. Taylor's work or testimony.

Suggested search terms for email and electronic files are "Elaine Taylor," "E. Taylor," "Taylor" within the same message as "lab" or "DNA," "Brady," "Giglio," and "crime lab."
I will pay copying costs as permitted by § 24A.5(4). No search fee may be charged "when the release of records is in the public interest," including release to taxpayers "seeking to determine whether those entrusted with the affairs of the government are honestly, faithfully, and competently performing their duties as public servants." 51 O.S. § 24A.5(4).
Requested Action
I ask the Office to take the following steps by October 14, 2026.
1. Withdraw the September 18, 2026, denial and search for records responsive to the request, beginning with the priority categories above.
2. Produce responsive records, or for each record withheld, identify the specific statutory exemption by section number.
3. Produce every reasonably segregable portion of any record withheld in part, as § 24A.5(3) requires.
4. Preserve all responsive records, including any eligible for destruction under 19 O.S. § 215.22, until this request is resolved.
If the Office has not withdrawn the denial by that date, I intend to seek review through the Public Access Counselor under 51 O.S. § 24A.40(B) and (D) and to consider an action under 51 O.S. § 24A.17.

Sincerely,

Jennifer Holtzclaw

MuckRock News, DEPT MR 199925 263 Huntington Ave. Boston, MA 02115 199925-35053988@requests.muckrock.com<mailto:199925-35053988@requests.muckrock.com>

Subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: Oklahoma County District Attorney Office Concerning OCPD Forensic Analyst Elaine Taylor Crime Lab Records
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

To whom it may concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, 51 O.S. §§ 24A.1 et seq., I hereby request access to and copies of records in the possession, custody, or control of the Oklahoma County District Attorney’s office concerning Elaine Taylor, a former forensic analyst with the Oklahoma City Police Department crime lab. This request includes crime lab records of a high-profile, controversial former government employee who has publicly admitted she destroyed forensic evidence and whose work is clearly in the public interest.

The Open Records Act is to be liberally construed in favor of disclosure, and any claimed exemption must be narrowly applied and strictly justified.

Title 51, Section 24A.7 (A) states that a "public body may keep personnel records confidential." (Emphasis added.) This provision does not mandate confidentiality of personnel records; the word “may” connotes discretion. (Mott v. Carlson, 1990 OK 10, 16 & n.4, 786 P.2d 1247, 1249 & n.4; Falconhead Prop. Owners Ass'n v. Fredrickson, 2002 ΟΚ CIV APP 67, 15, 50 P.3d 224, 226, Ross v. City of Owasso, 2017 OK CIV App 4, 389 P.3d 396, 400.)

Open records exemptions covered by Subsection A (1) and Subsection A(2) do not apply here. This request does not seek private information such as home addresses, telephone numbers, and social security numbers of past or current employees. § 24A.7(D). This request does not seek records pertaining to a current employee. Ms. Taylor retired in February 2017.

The request seeks public records regardless of format (paper, electronic, email, database entries, audit logs, attachments, or metadata) and covers the entirety of Ms. Taylor’s employment with OCPD, including any records in the possession of the District Attorney’s Office, created before, during, and after her active employment, whether maintained by the Crime Laboratory, Internal Affairs, Professional Standards, Human Resources, or any supervisory or administrative unit.

This request includes any and all records shared with any other outside entities pertaining to Ms. Taylor’s credibility, reliability, discipline, errors, misconduct, and forensic integrity.

These records include, but are not limited to:

Employment applications, resumes, hiring documents, and job descriptions

Dates of employment, assignments, promotions, demotions, or transfers

Performance evaluations, reviews, or appraisals

Training records, certifications, continuing education, and proficiency testing

Commendations, awards, or letters of recognition

Internal Affairs investigations, Professional Standards reviews, or administrative inquiries

Citizen complaints, prosecutorial complaints, judicial findings, or defense challenges

Disciplinary actions, counseling memoranda, reprimands, suspensions, or terminations

Findings of misconduct, negligence, error, or policy violations

Any investigations, whether formal or informal, that were sustained, not sustained, unfounded, or administratively closed
Retirement, resignation, or separation from employment

Exit interviews or separation memoranda

Post-employment restrictions, consulting agreements, or testimony disclosures
Any and all e-mails pertaining to the above listed items

In addition, this request covers all records reflecting issues related to forensic reliability or compliance, including:
Errors, mistakes, corrective actions, or remediation involving forensic testing or reporting

Nonconformities, deviations, or quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) issues

Testimony reviews, peer review critiques, technical review comments, or supervisory concerns

Corrective action reports, root-cause analyses, or retraining documentation

Any and all e-mails pertaining to the above listed items

These records also include Accreditation, Audit, and External Review Materials and other materials reflecting:

ASCLD/LAB, ANAB, or other accreditation audits referencing Elaine Taylor

External audits, inspections, or compliance reviews

Correspondence with accrediting bodies, prosecutors, or oversight agencies

Findings, warnings, or recommendations related to her work

Case reviews, retesting decisions, or post-conviction inquiries involving her forensic work

Notifications to prosecutors regarding credibility, reliability, or disclosure concerns

Brady, Giglio, or impeachment-related determinations or disclosures

Any and all e-mails pertaining to the above listed items, including any and all communications with District Attorneys, defense counsel, and courts concerning her work
If any portion of this request is denied or redacted, identify the specific statutory exemption relied upon, as required by 51 O.S. § 24A.5(4).

Please do not withhold entire documents where partial redaction is possible. Please ensure that all email, audit logs, and electronic systems are searched for responsive documents.

If records are maintained electronically, I request production in native electronic format where possible.

If the scope of this request can be narrowed to reduce cost or burden, please contact me before denying any portion of the request.
Please advise in advance of any copying or production costs exceeding $25.00. If fees are assessed, provide an itemized estimate pursuant to Oklahoma law.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Jennifer Holtzclaw

title: Utility Request Nov 2026

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: Utility Request Nov 2026
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

an export of public records concerning municipal water utility accounts that have experienced service disruptions due to non-payment or fire.
Specifically, I am requesting an electronic data export (preferably in CSV, Excel, or structured text format) of all residential and commercial water utility accounts that meet any of the following criteria within the past 120 days:
1. Accounts that have been physically disconnected or shut off for non-payment or fire.
2. Accounts where the meter has been locked out or pulled due to delinquency or fire.
3. Accounts currently on the final "scheduled for disconnect" or delinquency termination list.
To the extent available within your utility management system, please ensure the exported data fields include:
• Full Service Address (Street Number, Street Name, Unit, City, Zip Code)
• Disconnect, Lockout, or Shut-off Date
• Current Status Code / Account Status (e.g., Closed, Disconnected, Pending Shut-off)
Please note that I am not requesting individual customer payment histories, bank details, or Social Security numbers. If your department considers the outstanding dollar balance or individual customer names to be confidential or exempt under privacy guidelines, please redact only those specific fields and provide the rest of the structural location and status data.
As an electronic database export is requested, please provide these records in their native electronic format to avoid unnecessary printing or scanning fees.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

title: North Liberty Flock and Axon Agreements

communications.subject: Iowa Open Records Law Request: North Liberty Flock and Axon Agreements
communications.communication:
To the custodian of records:

Pursuant to Iowa Code Chapter 22, I request the following records of the City of North Liberty and the North Liberty Police Department.

1. All executed agreements with Flock Group, Inc. (dba “Flock Safety”), including contracts, memoranda of understanding, order forms, master services agreements, CJIS security addenda, deployment plans, and any attachments or documents incorporated by reference. This includes, without limitation:
  a. The purchase agreement and deployment plan signed in or about June 2024 by the department’s Patrol Lieutenant, as referenced in the police department’s June 2024 monthly report (July 9, 2024 council packet).
  b. Any “free trial,” pilot, or evaluation agreement (typically a memorandum of understanding) in effect before the service agreement.
  c. Any renewal, amendment, order form, or change order executed since the original agreement, including any document associated with Flock invoice INV-96173 (“Yearly Renewal,” $36,000, approved on the June 23, 2026 consent agenda).
2. The executed agreement currently in effect with Axon Enterprise, Inc. associated with invoice INUS452880 (“In-Car and Body Cameras Upgrade,” $68,034.39, approved on the June 23, 2026 consent agenda), described in the police department’s June 2026 monthly report (July 14, 2026 council packet) as a five-year contract covering in-car cameras, body-worn cameras, and associated software (including Draft One, Translate, and transcription). This includes any quote, order form, master services agreement, statement of work, and product or license schedule, together with any attachments or documents incorporated by reference.
3. All sole-source justifications, bid or quotation waivers, competitive-exception memoranda, or similar records associated with any agreement or contract for goods or services with Flock Group, Inc. or Axon Enterprise, Inc., together with the requisition or purchase order for each such agreement, including any explanation submitted under the City’s Purchasing Policy for why quotations or bids were not obtained.

This request seeks complete executed agreements, including signature pages, not unsigned drafts or proposals. Where no fully executed agreement is available, please provide the most recent proposed or draft version(s) and identify it as such. Please provide records in their original electronic format where possible.

These records are sought for discussion at the October 27, 2026 City Council meeting. If not all responsive records are available before that date, please release the records that are available and provide an estimated date for production of the remainder. If any record or portion thereof is withheld for any reason, including non-existence of a record, please identify what was withheld and the specific reason for its withholding.

Please contact me with any question about scope.

Sincerely,

HCvP

title: U.S. Secret Service: 1974 Counterfeiting Investigation and Arrest of Raymond C. Horsch (Doylestown/Bucks County, PA)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: U.S. Secret Service: 1974 Counterfeiting Investigation and Arrest of Raymond C. Horsch (Doylestown/Bucks County, PA)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request all investigative files, arrest records, seizure/evidence logs, laboratory or forensic reports on the counterfeit currency, Reports of Investigation, closing memoranda, and correspondence (including with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania) concerning the 1974 Secret Service investigation and arrest of Raymond C. Horsch for operation of a counterfeiting operation based in or near Doylestown, Bucks County,
Pennsylvania. Please construe "Doylestown" as the operation's base of activity rather than a strict jurisdictional limiter, as the arrest itself may have occurred at a different location within the Philadelphia Field Office's area of responsibility.

To assist in locating the case file and any cross-references:

● Subject name: Raymond Charles Horsch of Raymond Charles Hörsch (a.k.a. Raymond "R.C." Horsch)
● Date of birth: 1943 (deceased May 2025)
● Incident date/era: 1974
● Location: Doylestown / Bucks County, Pennsylvania (Philadelphia AOR)
● Offense: Manufacture/passing of counterfeit $10 Federal Reserve Notes; seizure reported at approximately $1 million face value; two-year federal sentence
● Later assumed identity (post-dates this case, offered only as a cross-reference aid): "Dr. Stanley Eugene Stokowski"

2. Fee Waiver Request

Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(iii), I request a full waiver of duplication and search fees. Disclosure is in the public interest because it will significantly contribute to public understanding of federal law enforcement operations and because Horsch's criminal history has become directly material to an active, widely reported Philadelphia missing-persons investigation centered on property he owned. I seek these records solely for non-commercial historical research and public education, and have no commercial interest in the material.

Should the above be only partially granted, I am willing to pay fees up to $25.00. Please contact
me before incurring any charges beyond that amount.

3. Expedited Processing Request

I additionally request expedited processing under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(E)(v)(II) and the corresponding DHS regulation. This request involves an urgency to inform the public about actual government activity, given that: (a) Horsch's decades-long criminal record — including this 1974 case — is currently the subject of active national and local news coverage tied to an ongoing homicide/missing-persons investigation; (b) records of his early federal criminal conduct bear directly on public assessment of how repeated prior law enforcement contact intersected with his later conduct; and (c) the story is developing in real time, making timely release materially more valuable to public understanding than a delayed release would be.

4. Deceased-Subject Privacy Considerations

The subject of this request, Raymond Charles Horsch, died in May 2025. Consistent with DOJ/OIP guidance, I recognize that death diminishes rather than eliminates privacy interests under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(6) and (b)(7)(C), and that third parties named in the file (agents, witnesses, co-conspirators) retain their own privacy interests independent of the subject's death. I am prepared to furnish documentation of death (e.g., published obituary or news account)
upon request to facilitate processing. Philadelphia media has been reporting widely on the death of Horsch and his unusual biography: https://archive.is/S6mOb

5. Records Disposition / NARA Contingency

Given that this case is now 52 years old, it is possible the underlying file has already been retired from USSS custody under the applicable records disposition schedule and transferred to the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), potentially under Record Group 87 (Records of the U.S. Secret Service). If USSS no longer holds these records, I ask that you identify the applicable disposition authority, accession number, or NARA location so that I may pursue the file directly with NARA, rather than receiving only a "no records" response.

6. Format, Segregability, and Exemptions

Please provide responsive records in electronic, text-searchable PDF format. If any portion is withheld, please cite the specific FOIA exemption applied to each withholding, release all reasonably segregable non-exempt material, and — for any records withheld in fuprovide sufficient descriptive detail (a Vaughn-style index) to allow me to evaluate the withholding.

Thank you for the work that the Secret Service does each and every day.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

Freedom of Information Act Program

File Number: 2026-USSSFOIA-01827 
Dear Requester: 

This letter acknowledges the receipt of your recent Freedom of lnformation Act (FOIA) request, received by the United States Secret Service (Secret Service) on 8/26/2026, for all investigative files, arrest records, seizure/evidence logs, laboratory or forensic reports on the counterfeit currency, Reports of Investigation, closing memoranda, and correspondence (including with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania), concerning the 1974 Secret Service investigation and arrest of Raymond C. Horsch for operation of a counterfeiting operation based in or near Doylestown, Bucks County, Pennsylvania. 

You have requested expedited processing of your request under the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) standard permitting expedition when a requester demonstrates a "compelling need." Your request for expedited treatment has been denied. 

Under the DHS/FOIA regulation, 6 C.F.R., Chapter I, Part 5 § 5.5, expedited processing of a FOIA request is warranted if the request involves "circumstances in which the lack of expedited treatment could reasonably be expected to pose an imminent threat to the life or physical safety of an individual" ((d)(l)(i)), or "an urgency to inform the public about an actual or alleged federal government activity, if made by a person primarily engaged in disseminating information" ((d)(l)(ii)). Requesters that seek expedited processing must submit a statement explaining, in detail, the basis for the request. Additionally, FOIA regulation, 6 C.F.R., Chapter I, Part 5 § 5.5(d)(3), requires that statements be certified, by the requester, to be "true and correct to the best of that person's knowledge and belief." 

Please be advised, your request has been denied because you do not qualify under either category. You have not demonstrated that there is a threat to the life or physical safety of an individual nor have you demonstrated there is a particular urgency to inform the public about the government activity involved in the request, beyond the public's right to know about government activity, generally. Your letter was conclusory, in nature, and did not present any facts to justify a grant of expedited processing under the applicable standards. 
If you deem the decision to deny expedited treatment to your request an adverse determination, you may exercise your appeal rights. Should you wish to file an administrative appeal, your appeal should be made in writing and received within sixty (60) days of the date of this letter, by writing to: Freedom oflnformation Appeal, Deputy Director, U.S. Secret Service, Communications Center, 245 Murray Lane, S.W., Building T-5, Washington, D.C. 20223. If you choose to file an administrative appeal, please explain the basis of your appeal and reference the case number listed above. 

Additionally, you have the right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation. Please note that contacting the Secret Service's FOIA Program and/or OGIS is not an alternative to filing an administrative appeal and does not stop the 90-day appeal clock. You may contact OGIS at: Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001. You may also reach OGIS via e-mail at ogis@nara.gov telephone at 202- 741-5770/toll free at (877) 684-6448, or facsimile at (202) 741-5769. 

Your request for a fee waiver will be held in abeyance pending the quantification of responsive records. The FOIA regulations, Title 6 C.F.R., Chapter I, Part 5 § 5.1l(k)(2)(3), set forth six factors to examine when determining whether the applicable legal standard for a fee waiver has been met. We will consider these factors: 

1) Whether the subject of the requested records concerns "the operations or activities of the government;" 
2) Whether the disclosure is "likely to contribute" to an understanding of government operations or activities; 
3) Whether disclosure of the requested information will contribute to the understanding of the public at large, as opposed to the individual understanding of the requestor or a narrow segment of interested persons; 
4) Whether the contribution of public understanding of government operations or activities will be "significant;" 
5) Whether the requester has a commercial interest that would be furthered by the requested disclosure; and 
6) Whether the magnitude of any identified commercial interest to the requestor is sufficiently large in comparison with the public interest in disclosure, that disclosure is primarily in the commercial interest of the requestor. 

In the event that your fee waiver is denied, we shall charge you for the records in accordance with FOIA regulations as they apply to non-commercial ("all other") requesters. The first 100 pages of duplication are free of charge. As an "all other" requester, you will be charged .10 cents a page for the duplication of each additional page. As an "all other" requester, the first 2 hours of search time are free of charge, after which you will be charged the per quarter-hour rate ($4.00, $7.00, $10.25) of the searcher. 
Furthermore, the submission of your request is viewed as an agreement, by you, to pay duplication and search time costs up to $25.00. A search for files responsive to your request is being conducted. The appropriate components of the Secret Service are being queried for responsive documents. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for a disclosure determination. You will be contacted before any additional fees are accrued. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. As your request seeks documents that will require a thorough and wide-ranging search, the Secret Service will invoke a 10-day extension for your request pursuant to 6 C.F.R., Part 5 § 5.5(c). If you would like to narrow the scope of your request, please contact our office. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. Additionally, per Section 5.5(a) of the FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R, Chapter I, Part 5, Secret Service processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. 

If you need any further assistance, or would like to discuss any aspect of your request, please contact our FOIA Public Liaison Kevin Tyrrell, at (202) 220-1819. Alternatively, you may send an e-mail to FOIA@usss.dhs.gov. FOIA File No. 2026-USSSFOIA-01827 is assigned to your request. Please refer to this file number in all future communication with this office. We solicit your cooperation and assure you that the search will be conducted as expeditiously as possible. 

Thank you,

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Request: 5 USC 552(a)(1,2) documents
communications.communication:
Dear FOIA department:

This is a FOIA request for all records described by 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(1, 2), as well as processing records for this request itself.

In particular, I request:

1. All:

a) descriptions of its central and field organization and the established places at which, the employees (and in the case of a uniformed service, the members) from whom, and the methods whereby, the public may obtain information, make submittals or requests, or obtain decisions;
b) statements of the general course and method by which its functions are channeled and determined, including the nature and requirements of all formal and informal procedures available;
c) rules of procedure, descriptions of forms available or the places at which forms may be obtained, and instructions as to the scope and contents of all papers, reports, or examinations;
d) substantive rules of general applicability adopted as authorized by law, and statements of general policy or interpretations of general applicability formulated and adopted by the agency; and
e) each amendment, revision, or repeal of the foregoing.

… except that you may, at your discretion, exclude records published in the Federal Register.

2. All:
a) final opinions, including concurring and dissenting opinions, as well as orders, made in the adjudication of cases;
b) those statements of policy and interpretations which have been adopted by the agency;
c) administrative staff manuals and instructions to staff that affect a member of the public;
d) copies of all records, regardless of form or format that have been requested 3 or more times; and
e) a general index of the records referred to under subparagraph (D); and
f) current indexes providing identifying information for the public as to any matter issued, adopted, or promulgated after July 4, 1967, and identified in paragraphs (A)-(E)

… except  that you may, at your discretion, exclude records published in the Federal Register, or available on your online FOIA reading room.



For the purposes of this request, all terms above have the same meaning as they do in 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(1, 2).



I also request:
3. all records relating to the fulfillment of this request

This part of the request is to be processed only AFTER you have completed processing all of the above parts. Do not conduct any search for records under this part earlier than that.

This part does not request that you create any new record; rather, it requests the records that you will have created in processing the above parts, and will therefore exist before you conduct the search for this part. See McGehee v. CIA, 697 F. 2d 1095, 1100-05 (D.C. Cir. 1983) (agency must use time-of-search cut-off date, not time-of-request).


For all responsive records, I also request:

1. all parts of the record (i.e. no portion of a record with some responsive portion may be considered "non-responsive");
2. all versions of the record, whether or not currently in use;
3. all record metadata, such as dates on which they were drafted, passed, went into effect, withdrawn, or similar events; person(s) / office(s) responsible; authors;  IDs; revision numbers; etc.;
4. a detailed index of all claims of exemption/privilege, regardless of whether the record is claimed to be exempt in whole or in part;
5. access to inspect the record directly, in its native electronic format; and
6. if any classification applies, mandatory declassification review (MDR) under E.O. 13526, and the result of the MDR, including any declassified records.

For all requests above, the "cut-off date" is, at the earliest, the date that you conduct the search.


Please note that this request is made after the enactment of Public Law No. 114-185, S. 337 (114th), the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 (FOIA IA). The revised statute, as specified in the FOIA IA, applies to this request. FOIA IA § 6. In particular, please note that:

1. you must provide electronic format documents, §§ 552(a)(2) (undesignated preceding text), 552(a)(2)(E) (undesignated following text), 552(a)(3)(B), and 552(a)(3)(C);
2. you may not specify an appeal duration less than 90 days, § 552(a)(6)(C)(A)(i)(III)(aa);
3. you may not withhold any record unless "the agency reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption described in subsection (b), or disclosure is prohibited by law", § 552(a)(8)(A)(i);
4. you must segregate and partially release records where possible, §§ 552(a)(8)(A)(ii) and 552(b) (undesignated matter following (b)(9)); and
5. you may not claim deliberative process exemption for records more than 25 years old, § 552(b)(5).


This request specifically excludes providing me with new copies of any records which have been already provided to me or published online for free (e.g. on the agency's online "reading room"), in full or identically to the form that would be provided to me under this request (i.e. with exactly the same format, redactions, and claimed exemptions).

This is only an exclusion on providing records under this request that are identical to those already provided to me or available online, and only if I am or have already been provided a link to the online version (if "available online").

This exclusion is only intended to limit unnecessary duplication or provision, not to limit what records are responsive to this request, nor to permit failure to disclose the location of a responsive record available online. If this exclusion would in any way increase the cost or duration to respond to this request, it is to be ignored to the extent it does so.


This request is to be treated as separate from all others that I have filed.


Please forward this request to the FOIA office of every agency component and subcomponent that may have responsive records for independent processing, with a copy to me.

This request includes any records held jointly by your agency in conjunction with any other agency and/or department, in interagency and/or interdepartmental systems of records, or by other agencies or third parties (including contractors) acting pursuant any agreement with your agency.


With the possible exception of the index of records claimed to be exempt or privileged, this request does not ask you to create new records. If you determine that a response would require creating a new record that you do not want to create, please first contact me by email with an explanation of what records you have that would most closely match the information requested and might be acceptable substitutes, so that we can reasonably tailor the request.

In particular, I specifically request that you do not create new documents in response to this request that are modifications of a digital record, such as page-view images, print views, scans, or the like. No such creation or substitution is authorized by FOIA or the Privacy Act.

However, if the same or similar records are held in both electronic and paper formats, this request includes both the paper and electronic versions. The paper version and the digital version are distinct records, and each may contain distinct information such as handwritten or other markings on the paper copy and embedded metadata in the electronic version.

Furthermore, to the extent that the native electronic format is proprietary or otherwise not in format accessible by widely available, open source software, I request that you also provide an export of the proprietary format into a standard, open format, as described below.


Please note that the FOIA requires you to service the maximum extent of my request that can be done via e.g. partial redaction of exempt material. If you believe some portions of a record to be exempt because it contains Sensitive Security Information (SSI,  49 CFR 15, 1520) or classified information (18 USC 798), please provide a version of the record redacted to the minimum extent necessary to remove exempt information (e.g. per  49 CFR 1520.15), along with adequate information to describe the reason for each specific exemption.


In order to help tailor my request, please provide an upfront estimate of the time and cost it will take to complete this request, broken down any significant factors that would affect cost to service, number of records in each category, and your estimate of how many records in the category are likely to be exempt.


Please provide me with incremental updates, with updated estimates for fulfillment of the remainder, rather than having the entirety of the request be blocked until fully completed.


In accordance with 5 USC 552(a)(3)(B, C) (E-FOIA), Rehabilitation Act § 508, and FOIA IA, please respond using native format, electronic, machine-processable, accessible, open, and well structured records to the maximum extent possible. This means, e.g.:

* native format records rather than PDFs or other conversions (note above re providing both native electronic records and scans of paper records, if both exist);
* individual files per distinct source record (e.g. one .msg file per email), named clearly using the record's identifier, title, and date, rather than a single file containing multiple concatenated records;
* records compliant with the Rehabilitation Act § 508, 36 CFR 1194.22, USAB ATBCB-2015-0002, and I​SO 14289­-1;
* fully digital text records rather than scans, rasterizations, or OCR;
* complete electronic records, as held on any computer (including phones, servers, backup servers, mail servers, workstations, etc.), including all headers and attachments, fully expanded e-mail addresses, full addresses for address "aliases", full lists for "distribution list" aliases, all embedded and external metadata, complete bitwise digital copies of the original file, all file headers, and all other file content;
* blackout rather than whiteout redactions, with every redaction marked with all exemption(s) claimed for that redaction;
* digital redactions rather than black marker or rasterization;
* lists and structured data as machine-processable spreadsheets (e.g. CSV, SQL, XSL) rather than word documents (e.g. DOC, PDF, TXT, RTF) or partial printouts (e.g. PDF);
* open format records (e.g. PDF, AVI, MPG) rather than proprietary format records (e.g. WordPerfect, Microsoft Advanced Systems Format (ASF)) (note above re providing both original, proprietary format records and open format records);
* scans rather than paper copies;
* digital audio/video files rather than physical tapes;
* upload to your Electronic Reading Room (or other publicly accessible server) rather than personal transfer (for all items other than the item requesting records related to me or my requests);
* email or (S)FTP file transfer rather than CD;
* email correspondence rather than physical mail; etc.

Multiple files may be sent in a combined, compressed form using standard ZIP, TAR, GZIP, BZIP2, and/or RAR formats, or sent as separate files, at your discretion.

However, do not use a password on any files, including ZIP files etc. If a password was present in the native format, leave it unaltered, send me the password.


If there are any files you prefer not to transfer by email (e.g. if they are more than 10MB), please upload them to me via the link listed below my signature.

Doing so is secure, completely free to you, and the files uploaded will go to me directly.


Please note that this request does not request that you physically "duplicate" records, as I do not want you to create any paper or other physical copy for me — I only want electronic versions (or scans, for records that are not fully available in electronic form). As such, I expect there to be no duplication related costs.

Furthermore, I specifically request access for inspection of the records, including direct electronic access, in native format, to any electronic records.


I am not currently willing to pay for servicing this request. I may be willing to pay if it is necessary; please send a detailed explanation of the costs and their statutory justification, and service the maximum extent of the request that can be done for free in the meantime.

I request that, pending fee waiver determination or appeal, you proceed with this request as if it were in the "other non-commercial requester" category.

This request is a qualified request for journalistic, public interest purposes (entitling me to fully waived fees). As such, I request public interest fee waiver and journalistic fee waiver.

1. I have no commercial interest in these records.

2. I am a representative of the news media and entitled to waiver of all search fees.

I intend and am able to host and publish all received records online to the general public at no charge, as well to publish highlights, analyses, summaries, commentaries, and other creative, original journalistic work about responsive records through multiple online publications, such as https://plus.google.com/+saizai, https://twitter.com/saizai, and https://s.ai/foia (among others).

I also have a standing agreement with BoingBoing to publish articles about these matters, under my byline, on boingboing.net.

I have previously made journalistic publication, extraction, commentary, and analysis based on my FOIA/PA requests, e.g. relating to TSA, DHS, DOJ, and USPS activities, which have gotten widespread public interest, attention, and comment, and resulted in secondary journalistic publications based on my original work. This includes publications such as The New York Times, Forbes, Bloomberg/BNA, ABC News/Fusion, RT America News, RightThisMinute, and BoingBoing. I intend to do the same with this request.

3. The records are of significant public interest, entitled to waiver of all duplication fees, since

a) as above, I both am able and intend to disseminate the files widely;
b) they would contribute greatly to the public understanding of the operations and activities of your agency, in that they are records that directly describe agency operations and activities, as well as the issues and matters described at the top of this letter;
c) they are not currently readily available;
d) their existence constitutes prima facie evidence of your agency's violation of Congress' explicit command in 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(1, 2) that your agency publish all the primary requested records; and
e) Congress has statutorily mandated that they be published freely, i.e. made a statutory finding that they are records of such significant public interest that they must be published without any request.

4. As mentioned above, I am explicitly not asking for any physical duplication, but rather direct server-to-server file transfer or email (or posting on your website). The FOIA authorizes duplication fees strictly limited to your agency's actual costs, and mandates that your agency use the cheapest available requested methods. I consider the actual costs for server-to-server file transfer to be reasonably estimated by, e.g., Amazon S3's pricing (https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/).


If you have any questions or updates about this request, please contact me by email.

Please ensure that all of your responses comply with § 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, 36 CFR 1194.22, and UESB NPRM ATBCB-2015-0002.

In particular, please make all correspondence pursuant to this request — including notification and responsive records — by email, with native electronic format records, as specified in the request. I do not authorize you to send anything to me by physical mail unless I specifically state otherwise.

My email address is sufficient for all response to this request, and I can provide you with free means of electronic transfer for records too large to email.

Do not respond using ZixCorp "Secure Mail" or any other method that "expires" records from being available. Use only actual email and direct attachments, unless I explicitly request otherwise.


Please let me know your tracking number(s) for this request upon receipt, as well as your specific estimated completion date. 5 USC 552(a)(7).

If you believe that any of the requested items are not reasonably described, or that you need any further information regarding my qualification for fee waivers, please be specific about what you consider vague and what questions I can answer that would clarify them.

This request is made via MuckRock. You may provide responsive records either directly to me (see below my sig), or via MuckRock, as described below.

Sincerely,
Sai				(Note: Sai is my full legal name; I am mononymic.)
President, SaiCorp, Inc.
SaiCorp is an organization devoted to public interest journalism, government transparency and accountability, individuals' civil rights, and related issues.

NOTE: This request is made on behalf of both myself, Sai (in personal capacity) and SaiCorp, Inc. (in official capacity).

Phone: +1 510 394 4724  (please leave voicemail if I do not pick up)
Email: foia@saizai.com
Upload link: https://www.dropbox.com/request/kbR4D5SjIrVxm1eE4uHn
Other identifiers for search purposes: "Sai", "saizai", "SaiCorp", "saizai.com", "s.ai", "i@s.ai", "legal@s.ai", "dccc@s.ai", "foia@saizai.com", "tsa@saizai.com", "saizai@gmail.com"
Physical mail: 500 Westover Dr. #4514, Sanford, NC 27330

NOTE: Do not physically mail responsive records without my explicit request. Send all records in native electronic form, as described above.

communications.communication:
Dear OPR -

1. Your response to part 1 of my request does not address the terms of the request. It specifically is directed at 552(a)(1) described records that have NOT been published as required by that statute.

Please provide all such records. If there are no responsive records because all records so described ARE published, then please respond by saying so.

2. You did not address part 2(e) of my request, which requires an "index" of (2)(d) records.

3. The form format of the records you provided does not match what was requested: native, electronic, § 508 accessible, separate files per source file, with metadata intact, etc. etc. as specifically described in the request.

What you provided is concatenated, rasterized scans, which my request explicitly calls out as not acceptable.

Please provide the records in the form and format requested.

Sincerely,
Sai

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Newton Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Newton Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

title: LOGIS - Minnesota data sharing with ICE via LexisNexis

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: LOGIS - Minnesota data sharing with ICE via LexisNexis
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

Context: LOGIS is a government entity and subject to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act (MGDPA) - Chapter 13. Our reporting has found that LexisNexis is a data broker with 175 million local police records from 2,400 unique law enforcement agencies across the United States. LexisNexis has an active contract to sell access to these local police records to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). ICE contracts with LexisNexis to gain access to local police's RMS, CAD, and JMS data, including LOGIS members where LOGIS facilitates the copying of information into LexisNexis's database. Seventy two Minnesota police departments are contributing data to this private LexisNexis database, some of which are LOGIS members and who have reported that LOGIS manages the integrations and data sharing with LexisNexis. Both ICE cooperation in Minnesota and public safety surveillance have been in the national news this year with significant public interest. We aim to better understand and report on these systems, and LOGIS's role in data sharing. 

To that end, we are requesting:

1) All emails between LOGIS and LexisNexis, including the domains: @lexisnexisrisk.com, @lexisnexis.com, and @lnssi.com. Timeframe: 6/1/2024 through 9/19/2026

2) From 1/1/2025 through 9/19/2026, please provide all emails in LOGIS systems that contain the terms "LexisNexis" or "Lexis Nexis" or "Accurint" or "AVCC" or "PSDEX" or "CommunityCrimeMap" or "Community Crime Map" - specifically we are looking for emails around how LOGIS handles local agency sharing decisions with LexisNexis, and how data sharing is revoked. If your search allows quotes, please use exact matching only for the search terms - wildcards or partial matching for 'Community Crime Map' can yield thousands of unnecessary results. 

3) If you coordinate the response to this public records request with LexisNexis in any way, please include the associated emails, text messages, call logs, or similar logs of your communication with LexisNexis. Please include any notice given to LexisNexis regarding this request. I note that a vendor's objection does not alter the classification of government data under Chapter 13.

Request Details:
- Format: .eml, .msg, .mbox, .pst, or other native / original copies of emails are preferred. Please include emails in original state. 
- Include: Attachments, embedded photos, links, subjects, to/from, and other email details in original state.
- Exclude: Some agencies receive an email every time a successful import is completed into LexisNexis's system, resulting in thousands of emails per year. If you receive these type of repeat, bulk emails, please include a sample of ten, but you do not need to include hundreds or thousands of the same emails. If you send an email count or time estimate, please exclude these bulk emails. 
- If you withhold or redact any responsive documents, please cite the specific code as required by § 13.03, subd. 3(f)

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: RE: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: LOGIS - Minnesota data sharing with ICE via LexisNexis
communications.communication:
While LOGIS did assist with creating the integration between some LOGIS members and LexisNexis many years ago, we do not directly share or coordinate the sharing of information with them. Only the members can authorize and execute the sharing of their information. You will need to contact the applicable public safety agencies for any data sharing or communications they may have made.

Chris Miller
Executive Director

communications.subject: RE: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: LOGIS - Minnesota data sharing with ICE via LexisNexis
communications.communication:
Mr. Miller,

Thank you for the reply. I will contact the member agencies directly about how their sharing with LexisNexis was originally set up.

Your response speaks to who authorizes data sharing. My request was for the emails LOGIS itself holds, and it stands as written. LOGIS is a joint powers organization and, as your FAQ notes, a government entity under Minn. Stat. § 13.02, subd. 7a and 11. Communications LOGIS created, received, or maintains are government data under subd. 7 regardless of which party authorizes the sharing. That includes correspondence about the integrations LOGIS built for its members.

Two clarifications:

1. I am aware of at least one member agency that contacted LOGIS about LexisNexis during the period covered by my request. This leads me to believe there will be at least one email containing these search terms. 

2. Please treat tickets in the help desk or ticketing systems your members use to reach LOGIS as within scope of items 1 and 2, alongside email.

If LOGIS responds that it has no responsive data, I will understand that to mean LOGIS searched its email and ticketing systems and found no messages to or from the three listed domains, and none whose subject or body contains the listed terms, within the stated timeframes. If any responsive data are withheld, please cite the specific statutory basis as required by § 13.03, subd. 3(f).

I appreciate your help and look forward to the records.

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: RE: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: LOGIS - Minnesota data sharing with ICE via LexisNexis
communications.communication: Thanks for the clarification. I have submitted a support ticket to assess the number of positive hits using the search terms you requested. I will follow up with an estimate of costs associated with complying with the request.

communications.subject: RE: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: LOGIS - Minnesota data sharing with ICE via LexisNexis
communications.communication:
Good evening.

In regards to our ticketing system, there were no positive matches that came back when we searched the system using the search terms noted below. With regard to out emails, we found the following:


  *   19,000+ matches within our email system. When we reviewed some samples, it appears that at least some were automated emails from LexisNexis regarding data imports/exports.
  *   26,000+ matches on a file server that we named “Accurint”, which of course was one of the search terms. When we reviewed some samples, there were many emails related to that server (such as network alerts on that server) that appear in the results



Please confirm if you want us to attempt to generate copies of the 45,000+ emails or other positive matches that appear in our system; OR if you would like to refine the search terms. To be clear, I have not inquired as to the time and cost of fulfilling this request, but we do intend to charge you an hourly billing rate for the individual(s) associated with searching and compiling the records. We will await your response before proceeding. Thank you.



Chris Miller

communications.subject: RE: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: LOGIS - Minnesota data sharing with ICE via LexisNexis
communications.communication:
Mr. Miller,

Thanks for running the search and for the quick turnaround. 45,000 is far more than I need, and most of it sounds like noise. Let me narrow.

Please exclude:
- Automated emails from LexisNexis about data imports or exports. A sample of 10 is plenty.
- Network alerts, monitoring messages, and other system-generated notices that mention the "Accurint" file server. Same here: a sample of 5 is enough.
- Anything sent from a no-reply address generally.

What I am after is person-to-person email:
1) Emails between LOGIS staff and a person at LexisNexis (the three domains) on any topic: account management, sales or marketing, support, contracts, integration setup, or server and IT issues. 6/1/2024 through 9/19/2026.
2) Emails between LOGIS staff and member agency staff that mention LexisNexis, Accurint, AVCC, PSDEX, or Community Crime Map, including how sharing was set up, questions about it, or requests to change or stop it. 1/1/2025 through 9/19/2026.

Filtering out automated senders first and then deduplicating should get most of the way there. My guess is the human correspondence is a few dozen messages at most. If you can share the count after that filter, I am happy to narrow further before anyone starts compiling.

On cost: I understand LOGIS may charge for staff time under § 13.03, subd. 3(c). I would ask LOGIS to consider waiving or reducing the fee. This is a non-commercial request, the records will be published, and the subject (local police data reaching ICE through LexisNexis) is of real public interest in Minnesota right now. The narrowing above should also cut the staff time considerably. If a waiver is not possible, please send the estimate before proceeding and I will adjust scope to fit.

Thanks again for your help with this.

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: New Jersey Open Public Records Act Request: Public-records request — OCR case 02-22-1153 monitoring records (Jan. 1, 2025–present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Jersey Open Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Please provide electronic copies of records maintained by PLUMSTED TOWNSHIP SCHOOL DISTRICT from January 1, 2025 through the date of this request concerning the U.S. Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights (OCR) resolution agreement in OCR case 02-22-1153.

I request the following existing records:

1. District correspondence with OCR about the identified agreement or case, including messages to or from OCR-Transition@ed.gov, the OCR staff addresses identified in the Agreement or Letter, and other Department of Education addresses ending in @ed.gov when the message concerns this case, agreement, or a related monitoring submission. This includes OCR acknowledgments, feedback, approvals, requests for revision or additional information, closure-related messages, and any bounced, undeliverable, rejected, failed-delivery, out-of-office, automated-reply, non-delivery, or other delivery-status messages, as well as follow-up messages or internal records indicating that an attempted OCR contact or submission did not receive a response. Include attachments and transmittal emails.
2. Records submitted, prepared for submission, or maintained for submission to OCR, including reports, data, policies, training materials, remediation records, implementation updates, requests for approval, transmittal emails, and records identifying deliverables, deadlines, or responsible staff.
3. Internal district emails or memoranda about an inability to reach OCR, delivery failures, unacknowledged submissions, unanswered follow-ups, delayed OCR feedback or approval, delayed submission, or delayed agreement work.

If no responsive records exist, please state that explicitly. If any portion is withheld, please identify the specific exemption and release all reasonably segregable portions.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Meredith Kolodner

communications.subject: RE: New Jersey Open Public Records Act Request: Public-records request — OCR case 02-22-1153 monitoring records (Jan. 1, 2025–present)
communications.communication:
Dear Mr. Ytreboe,

t's now November 4, and I appreciate your response but it doesn’t meet the requirements of the Open Public Records Act.

Under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), a custodian who is unable to comply with a request “shall indicate the specific basis therefor.” Your response states only " If your request is not responded to by November 4, 2026, it
shall be deemed denied." It does not identify the statute, regulation, executive order, or other authority relied on, and it does not state which of my request items it applies to.

Please provide within five business days a supplemental written response that:

1) addresses each item in my request separately;
2) cites the specific statutory or regulatory exemption for any record withheld in full, and explains why it applies;
under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), discloses the remainder of any record that is partly exempt, and identifies each redaction and its legal basis;
3) states whether any responsive records exist that you have not located or reviewed; and
identifies any records withheld under a common-law privilege.

I also note that under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-6, the agency bears the burden of proving that a denial of access is authorized by law, and that N.J.S.A. 47:1A-8 preserves my common law right of access to these records. I request that you consider access on that basis as well.


Sincerely,
Meredith Kolodner, The Hechinger Report
917-881-3896

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Boston Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)
